description:
A statement: the transactions of one account (account_uid), of every account on one consent (label), or of every account on every stored consent (neither), following the bank's pagination to the end. Each account read spends one of the few reads the bank allows per account per day (about four), so read once and narrow with the filters rather than reading again: text, direction, amount_min and amount_max run here, after the read, and cost nothing more.

Dates are YYYY-MM-DD and empty means unbounded. transaction_status takes a friendly name (booked, pending, cancelled, hold, other, rejected, scheduled) or a PSD2 code; empty omits the filter, which is NOT the same as asking for booked.

Each row carries a SIGNED decimal amount as a string, negative for money leaving the account, and a counterparty resolved against the direction rather than copied from one fixed field. Amounts are strings because they are exact: parse them yourself if you need arithmetic. An amountWarning appears only on a row whose figure could not be taken at face value. Reading several accounts, each row also names its account, and one account that fails is reported in accounts without hiding the others. For more rows than a reply should hold, export_transactions writes the same statement as CSV.

account_uid.description: One account: the uid field from list_accounts (a UUID, not the IBAN). Leave out to read every account on a consent.

amount_max.description: Keep rows of at most this size, sign ignored.

amount_min.description: Keep rows of at least this size, sign ignored, as a plain decimal such as "250" or "1200.50".

direction.description: credit: money in; debit: money out.

label.description: Every account on this stored consent (a label from list_stored_sessions). Leave out, with account_uid, to read every stored consent.

text.description: Keep rows whose counterparty name or IBAN, payment reference or entry reference contains this; case and diacritics ignored.

name: get_transactions
